title: Change a field on a custom setting's default organization value
when: The step asks to change a field (usually a checkbox or a value) on a hierarchy custom setting, such as a managed package's 'Org Parameters' or 'Platform Settings', at the organization level. It is not creating a custom setting, not editing its definition or fields, and not a custom metadata type.
steps: The embedded Custom Settings page lists every setting, many pages long, and has no search box. Above the list is an A-Z row of letter links: click the letter the setting's label starts with (for example 'O' for Org Parameters).
Several packages can have a setting with the same label. Pick the row whose Namespace Prefix matches the package the step names (for example 'loan'), and click 'Manage' in that row.
On the setting's page, click 'Edit' in the Default Organization Level Value section. Do not click 'New', and do not edit a profile or user level row.
Change only the field the step names, to the value it asks for.
doneWhen: The setting's Default Organization Level Value section, in its read-only view, shows the named field with the requested value.

verified.outcome: Recipe matched with --candidates; 5 actions, 37 s: letter 'O', Manage in the Org Parameters row with namespace loan, Edit, Production unticked, Save. Reviewer confirmed Production [Not Checked]; independently, SOQL on loan__Org_Parameters__c returned loan__Production__c = false. No Setup Audit Trail entry, as expected for custom setting data.

notes: Proven on a real sandbox rather than by a trial: it needs a package's hierarchy custom setting a scratch org does not have. Written after a run where the agent could not find 'Org Parameters' among hundreds of managed settings: the letter row was on screen but not used. Custom setting data changes leave no Setup Audit Trail entry, so only the page reviewer can judge the result.
